subtopics.content: Alphabetization, spelling, rules of word merger and division, punctuation and paragraphing in line with standard Hausa.
subtopics.objective: Recognize the basic Hausa orthographical rules; apply the Hausa orthographical rules; identify linguistic errors such as grammatical errors, wrong choice of words and wrong spelling.

subtopics.content: Contextual questions from short unseen passages of about 200 words.
subtopics.objective: Read written Hausa texts; comprehend Hausa text in a given context; interpret various meanings and functions of words in a given text; acquire sufficient vocabulary; recognize central issues in a given text; draw conclusions based on available evidence in a given text.

subtopics.content: Argumentative, descriptive, dialogue, expository, narrative and letter writing.
subtopics.objective: Acquire the knowledge and techniques of composition writing in Hausa; recognize the different segments of composition in Hausa; recognize the different types of Hausa composition.

subtopics.content: Types of translation (Ire-iren fassara); rules of translation (Ƙa’idojin fassara); problems of translation (Matsalolin fassara); techniques of translation (Dabarun fassara).
subtopics.objective: Translate proverbial and idiomatic expressions and new words from English to Hausa; recognize the different types of translation; understand the basic techniques of translating proverbial and idiomatic expressions and new words into Hausa; identify the problems of translation into Hausa.

subtopics.content: Consonants: production and classification in terms of phonation, place and manner of articulation.
subtopics.objective: Analyse the process of sound production and combination of sounds to form meaningful words in Hausa; distinguish between the phonetic attributes of sounds.

subtopics.content: Vowels: production and classification in terms of position of tongue and lips; monophthongs and diphthongs.
subtopics.objective: Appraise the importance of vowels in determining meaning; distinguish between the phonetic attributes of sounds.

subtopics.content: Tone, including high, low and falling tones.
subtopics.objective: Analyse the process of sound production and combination of sounds to form meaningful words in Hausa; distinguish between the phonetic attributes of sounds.

subtopics.content: Syllable structure and types, including open and closed syllables, light and heavy syllables, and word categories such as monosyllabic and disyllabic words.
subtopics.objective: Recognize the number of syllables and their types in a word.

subtopics.content: Vowel length, including long and short vowels.
subtopics.objective: Appraise the importance of vowels in determining meaning; distinguish between the phonetic attributes of sounds.

subtopics.content: Phonological processes, including assimilatory processes such as palatalization, labialization and vowel harmony, and non-assimilatory processes such as insertion and deletion.
subtopics.objective: Analyse phonological processes in Hausa.

subtopics.content: Roots and stems of Hausa words.
subtopics.objective: Explain the roots and stems of Hausa words.

subtopics.content: Affixation, including prefixes, infixes and suffixes, and their derivational and inflectional functions.
subtopics.objective: Explain the inflectional process in Hausa word formation; explain the derivational process of word formation in Hausa; differentiate between the two morphological processes.

subtopics.content: Gender and number inflections.
subtopics.objective: Explain the inflectional process in Hausa word formation; differentiate between inflectional and derivational morphological processes.

subtopics.content: Derivation of nouns and adjectives from verbs, and adjectives and verbs from nouns.
subtopics.objective: Explain the derivational process of word formation in Hausa; differentiate between the two morphological processes.

subtopics.content: Word classes, including nouns, pronouns, verbs, adverbs, adjectives, prepositions, conjunctions, interjections and ideophones.
subtopics.objective: Analyse the processes governing word combination to form phrases, clauses and sentences in Hausa; detect linguistic errors in grammar; construct grammatical sentences for effective communication.

subtopics.content: Grammatical categories, including tense and aspect (general and relative past, general and relative continuous, first and second future, habitual); mood (subjunctive and negative); gender (masculine, feminine and neuter); and number (singular and plural).
subtopics.objective: Use appropriate tenses in spoken and written Hausa; use appropriate gender and number in spoken and written Hausa; detect linguistic errors in grammar.

subtopics.content: Sentence structure, including verbal sentences; nominal phrase plus verbal phrase and their components; non-verbal sentences consisting of nominal phrase plus stabilizer, nominal phrase plus complement plus stabilizer, and nominal phrases plus continuous frame (yana/yake) with or without da plus nominal phrase.
subtopics.objective: Analyse the processes governing word combination to form phrases, clauses and sentences in Hausa; recognize ideas or thoughts in written form; construct grammatical sentences for effective communication; distinguish between nominal and verbal phrases.

subtopics.content: Sentence types, including simple, compound and complex sentences.
subtopics.objective: Distinguish between types of sentence structure; distinguish between types of sentences; construct grammatical sentences for effective communication.

subtopics.content: Clauses, including relative and subjunctive clauses, and their functions as main and subordinate clauses.
subtopics.objective: Compare types of clauses; analyse the processes governing word combination to form phrases, clauses and sentences in Hausa.

subtopics.content: Lexical aspects of word meaning, including ambiguity, synonyms and antonyms.
subtopics.objective: Analyse the mechanisms of generating meanings in Hausa; build vocabulary; recognize the various meanings and functions of sentences in communication.

subtopics.content: Figures of speech and specialized meanings of words and phrases, including idioms and proverbs.
subtopics.objective: Analyse the mechanisms of generating meanings in Hausa; use words and sentences suitable for a particular purpose; construct meaningful sentences for effective communication.

subtopics.content: Birth (haihuwa): conception, pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding, customs during the first week after birth, bathing, ɓanti, weaning, circumcision and adolescence.
subtopics.objective: Explain the customs associated with conception through adolescence; explain the influence of modern times on childbirth and related customs.

subtopics.content: Marriage (aure): types of marriage, courtship, engagement, marriage solemnization, wedding celebrations, married life, divorce and widowhood.
subtopics.objective: Explain customs from courtship through widowhood; explain the influence of modern times on marriage.

subtopics.content: Death (mutuwa): announcement of death, washing of the deceased, funeral prayers, burial, mourning, charity, widowhood and inheritance.
subtopics.objective: Explain customs and practices associated with death, mourning and inheritance; explain the influence of modern times on death-related customs.

subtopics.content: The influence of modern times on Hausa customs and ways of life.
subtopics.objective: Identify and explain the different forms of modern influence on Hausa customs.

subtopics.content: Family structure, the gandu system, relationships between co-wives, kinship, slavery and agolanci.
subtopics.objective: Explain the structure of relationships and interactions within the family; explain the importance of social relationships among the Hausa.

subtopics.content: Neighbourly relationships (maƙwabtaka).
subtopics.objective: Explain the importance of social relationships and interactions among the Hausa.

subtopics.content: Communal labour and cooperative work, including aikin gandu and aikin gayya.
subtopics.objective: Explain the importance of social relationships and communal cooperation among the Hausa.

subtopics.content: Friendship and alliances (abota da ƙawance).
subtopics.objective: Explain the structure and importance of social relationships among the Hausa.

subtopics.content: Greetings and hospitality (gaisuwa da karamci).
subtopics.objective: Explain the importance of social relationships and interactions among the Hausa.

subtopics.content: The influence of modern times on social relationships and institutions.
subtopics.objective: Identify the different forms of modern influence on Hausa social customs.

subtopics.content: Types of traditional occupations, including farming, blacksmithing, tanning, trading, traditional barbering, carving, hunting, leatherwork, weaving, hairdressing, dyeing, butchery and fafar ƙorai, among others.
subtopics.objective: Identify traditional occupations; identify the characteristics and practices of people engaged in these occupations; distinguish occupations associated with men and women.

subtopics.content: Characteristics of traditional occupations, including methods of inheritance, tools and equipment, stages of production, and their importance.
subtopics.objective: Identify the methods by which occupations are inherited; describe the tools and equipment used; explain the importance of traditional occupations.

subtopics.content: Products and benefits of traditional occupations.
subtopics.objective: Identify products made through traditional occupations; describe their uses and benefits.

subtopics.content: Traditional occupational titles and ranks.
subtopics.objective: Identify traditional occupational titles and explain their significance.

subtopics.content: Occupations associated with gender, including domestic service and wage labour, hairdressing and barbering.
subtopics.objective: Distinguish occupations associated with men and women; describe traditional occupational practices.

subtopics.content: The influence of modern times on traditional occupations.
subtopics.objective: Identify and explain the influence of modern times on traditional occupations.

subtopics.content: Household necessities, including clothing and household utensils.
subtopics.objective: Identify Hausa material culture and household necessities; explain their uses and importance.

subtopics.content: Other material necessities, including buildings and food preparation.
subtopics.objective: Identify material necessities used by the Hausa and explain their uses.

subtopics.content: The influence of modern times on material culture and everyday necessities.
subtopics.objective: Identify and explain the influence of modern times on Hausa material culture.

topics.title: Bukukuwa da Wasanni (Hausa Festivities and Recreational Activities)

subtopics.content: Religious festivities, including Eid celebrations, takutaha (sallar gani), cikaciki and saukar karatu.
subtopics.objective: Identify Hausa festivities and recreational activities; explain their importance and how they are conducted; describe ways to preserve them; explain the influence of modern times on festivities.

subtopics.content: Traditional festivities, including kalankuwa, buɗar dawa and the pumpkin-eating festival.
subtopics.objective: Identify traditional festivities; explain their importance and how they are conducted; describe ways to preserve them.

subtopics.content: Occupational festivities and activities, including fishing festivals, dambe, kokawa, hunting games, blacksmiths’ games and hawan ƙaho.
subtopics.objective: Identify occupational festivities and recreational activities; explain their importance, methods of performance and preservation.

subtopics.content: Entertainment activities, including horse riding (sukuwa).
subtopics.objective: Identify recreational activities and explain their importance and methods of performance.

subtopics.content: Children’s games, including shalle, kulli-kurciya, a-sharuwan-tsuntsaye, gaɗa and carafke.
subtopics.objective: Identify children’s games; explain how they are played and their importance; describe ways to preserve them.

subtopics.content: The influence of modern times on Hausa festivities and recreational activities.
subtopics.objective: Explain the influence of modern times on festivities and games.

topics.title: Camfe-camfe da Bauta (Traditional Beliefs and Worship)

subtopics.content: Traditional beliefs and superstitions, including kangida, camfi, kambun baka and maita.
subtopics.objective: Identify different traditional beliefs and the methods through which they are practised; explain their perceived benefits and disadvantages; explain the influence of modern times on them.

subtopics.content: Traditional worship, including bori and tsafi.
subtopics.objective: Identify traditional forms of worship and their practices; explain their perceived benefits and disadvantages.

subtopics.content: The influence of modern times on traditional beliefs and worship.
subtopics.objective: Explain the influence of modern times on traditional beliefs and worship.

subtopics.content: Traditional authorities, including rulers, hakimai, dagatai and ward heads.
subtopics.objective: Identify traditional offices and ranks; describe the hierarchy of offices; identify the duties and importance of each office.

subtopics.content: Royal servants and officials, including shantali, jakadiya and baraya.
subtopics.objective: Identify traditional offices and ranks; explain the duties and importance of each position.

subtopics.content: Positions associated with religion, including imam and judge (alƙali).
subtopics.objective: Identify religiously associated offices; explain their duties and importance.

subtopics.content: The duties and responsibilities of traditional authorities and officials.
subtopics.objective: Identify the duties and importance of each traditional office.

subtopics.content: The influence of modern times on traditional authority.
subtopics.objective: Explain the influence of modern times on traditional offices and authority.

subtopics.content: Types of traditional medicine, including traditional preparations such as sassaƙe-sassaƙe, sawyoyi, na gari and na ruwa.
subtopics.objective: Classify the different types of traditional medicine.

subtopics.content: Religious or spiritual remedies, including amulets (layu), written charms (rubutu), ɗibbu and divination (duba).
subtopics.objective: Classify traditional and religious forms of medicine and remedies.

subtopics.content: Methods of administering traditional medicine, including drinking, rubbing, surace, fumigation or perfuming, inhaling, chewing, sucking, tying, sticking and hanging.
subtopics.objective: Describe the different methods of using traditional medicine.

subtopics.content: Dosage and measurement in the use of traditional medicine.
subtopics.objective: Explain the procedures for measuring and administering traditional medicine.

subtopics.content: Functions of traditional medicine, including prevention and treatment.
subtopics.objective: Explain the purposes and uses of traditional medicine.

subtopics.content: The influence of modern times on traditional medicine.
subtopics.objective: Explain the influence of modern times on traditional medicine.

subtopics.content: Oral narratives, including tatsuniya, almara, hikaya, ƙissa, historical narratives and other forms of oral storytelling.
subtopics.objective: Identify and distinguish the types of oral narratives; use appropriate vocabulary when discussing a story.

topics.title: Adabin Baka (Oral Literature): Maganganun Azanci (Folk Sayings)

subtopics.content: Folk sayings and verbal art, including take, kirari, habaici, zambo, karin magana, kacici-kacici, salon magana and adon magana.
subtopics.objective: Identify the forms of folk sayings and explain how they are used; memorize and use appropriate expressions associated with folk sayings.

topics.title: Adabin Baka (Oral Literature): Waƙoƙi na Baka (Oral Songs)

subtopics.content: Types of oral songs, including court songs, communal songs, men's songs, love songs and other categories.
subtopics.objective: Identify the different types of oral songs; identify the people who perform the different types of songs.

subtopics.content: The theme, style, form, structure, performer, musical instruments and subject of oral songs.
subtopics.objective: Distinguish the form, theme, style, structure and instruments used in oral songs; identify the performers and subjects of the songs.

subtopics.content: Work songs, including songs for grinding, pounding, threshing and hawking.
subtopics.objective: Identify the types of work songs and the people who perform them.

subtopics.content: Children’s songs for boys and girls, wedding songs and dandali songs.
subtopics.objective: Identify and distinguish the forms of children’s songs and other specified oral songs.

topics.title: Adabin Baka (Oral Literature): Wasannin Kwaikwayo na Gargajiya (Traditional Drama)

subtopics.content: Traditional children's drama, including langa, wasan ’yartsana, tashe, wasan gauta, dokin kara and other forms.
subtopics.objective: Identify the forms of traditional drama; explain how traditional dramatic performances are conducted; explain their importance; distinguish children's drama from adult drama.

subtopics.content: Methods of performing traditional children's drama and its importance.
subtopics.objective: Explain the methods of conducting traditional drama and identify its importance.

subtopics.content: Traditional adult drama, including ’yan kama, kalankuwa, hoto, wowwo and tashe.
subtopics.objective: Identify the forms of traditional adult drama; explain how they are performed and their importance; distinguish adult drama from children's drama.

subtopics.content: Prescribed prose text: Maraya by I. A. Mahe.
subtopics.objective: Analyse the form, structure, theme, style and characters in the prescribed prose text; understand and observe Hausa writing conventions; understand word and sentence meanings to comprehend the story; identify important messages in the story and draw conclusions about it.

subtopics.content: Prescribed poetry text: Waƙoƙin Wayar Da Kai Don Manazarta Hausa Na Ɗaya by A. Anwar.
subtopics.objective: Understand and analyse the theme, style, form and structure of the prescribed poem; observe writing conventions, particularly those of poetry; interpret word and sentence meanings; relate the use of words and sentences to the message of the poem; identify important messages and draw conclusions about the poem.

subtopics.content: Prescribed drama text: Malam Zalimu by A. H. Gidan Dabino.
subtopics.objective: Analyse the setting, theme, style, characters, form and structure of the prescribed play; understand the importance of writing conventions in conveying meaning; understand word meanings to comprehend the play; identify important messages in the play and draw conclusions about them.
